cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A CDN caches responses in edge locations (PoPs) close to users, so most requests never reach the origin. Users are routed to the nearest PoP by anycast or GeoDNS.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: On a miss the PoP fetches from the origin, often through an origin shield so the origin sees about one request per object, and caches for the s-maxage TTL. Keep the cache key minimal, version static URLs, purge by tag, prefer soft purge. Watch for cache poisoning and cache deception.

questions.a: To cache longer at the CDN, which you can purge, than in browsers, which you cannot.

questions.q: CDN hit ratio fell from 90 to 20 percent after a release. What do you check?
questions.a: New cookies or Set-Cookie, new query params in the key, Vary changes, missing Cache-Control, or a policy change.
An unkeyed header the origin reflects gets cached and served to everyone. Strip unknown headers and keep unkeyed inputs out of responses.
